newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Pao de Acucar share issue raises $150 mln.
newsitem.headline: Pao de Acucar share issue raises $150 mln.

text.p: Brazil's Pao de Acucar supermarket chain said it raised $150 million with its new share issue via a Level Three ADR program.
The company said in a statement it sold 7.5 million American Depositary Shares (ADS). Each ADS represents 1,000 preferred shares. The firm made its debut on the New York Stock Exchange on May 29.
The supermarket chain had expected to raise $130 million, but it increased the offer due to higher demand, it said.
Pao de Acucar, formally known as Companhia Brasileira de Distribuicao, was the first Brazilian retailer to list its stock on the NYSE.
The company said the listing will allow the group to speed up expansion plans and reach individuals and not only institutional investors.

Pao de Acucar became publicly traded in October 1995 with the sale of 10.2 billion preferred shares, or 14.6 percent of the company's total capital. The money raised with the share issue is being used to finance its 730 million reais investment plan for the 1996/1998 period.
